candidate.blueprint_locator: Safe and Effective Care Environment — Management of Care: coordinate interdisciplinary care, use specialized resources, and support evidence-based systems that improve client outcomes.
candidate.blueprint_topic: Management of Care — organized stroke-unit care
candidate.educational_objective: Recognize organized inpatient stroke-unit care as a multidisciplinary care model associated with improved survival, independence, and discharge/home-living outcomes compared with conventional ward care.

options.A: Greater likelihood of survival, independence, and living at home after follow-up because organized stroke-unit care integrates specialized multidisciplinary assessment, treatment, and rehabilitation.
options.B: No meaningful difference in survival or independence compared with conventional ward care once acute reperfusion decisions are complete.
options.C: Worse functional outcomes because geographically colocated stroke units delay rehabilitation and multidisciplinary care.
options.D: A shorter hospital stay is the main proven benefit, whereas mortality and disability outcomes are unchanged.

candidate.rationale: A is correct. The 2026 AHA/ASA acute ischemic stroke guideline states that organized inpatient stroke-unit care reduces death, disability, and institutionalization. The supporting systematic review found that patients cared for in organized stroke units were more likely to survive, be independent, and live at home at follow-up; benefits were seen across age, sex, stroke type, and severity. B and C contradict this evidence. D is incorrect because the guideline notes no clear effect on length of stay while showing better survival and independence outcomes.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Organized inpatient stroke-unit care improves clinically important outcomes such as survival and independence relative to conventional ward care and is characterized by coordinated specialized multidisciplinary management.
candidate.source_document_title: 2026 Guideline for the Early Management of Patients With Acute Ischemic Stroke
candidate.source_locator: Section 5.1 Stroke Units — Synopsis: organized stroke-unit care reduces death, disability, and institutionalization; key characteristics include specialized multidisciplinary care, caregiver involvement, staff specialization, early/intensive therapy, and treatment protocols. Recommendation-Specific Supportive Text: updated systematic review of 29 trials/5902 participants found patients in organized inpatient stroke units more likely to survive, be independent, and live at home, with no clear effect on length of stay.
candidate.source_organization: American Heart Association / American Stroke Association
candidate.stem: A client with acute ischemic stroke is admitted to an organized inpatient stroke unit rather than a general medical ward. Which outcome is most consistent with current evidence?
